1.support: Our primary objective was to compare OP values determined by five distinct methods

2.support: Patients aged 18 years or older who had moderate to severe ARDS according to the Berlin classification were included... Exclusion criteria included contraindications to EIT

3.support: We conducted a prospective physiological study in ARDS patients admitted to the medical ICUs at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok

4.support: Among thirty-nine patients, twenty-six were eligible. Four patients were excluded due to hemodynamic instability during RM, and one patient had incomplete EIT data

5.support: Sample size was calculated a priori in G*Power... a total of 20 participants was required... the achieved power was 0.88

6.support: PEEP was decreased from 20 cm H2O to 8 cm H2O in 2 cm H2O steps at one-minute intervals
6.location: Page 3, Section 2.2.3 Recruitment maneuver and decremental PEEP titration

7.support: The following criteria characterized the potential risk of VILI at the optimum PEEP: 1) The airway plateau pressure > 30 cm H2O... 5) The percentage of lung collapse by EIT

8.support: The report describes no blinding of the personnel assessing EIT, Ptp, or hemodynamic outcomes, and in this physiological study the operators performing titration were necessarily the assessors.
8.location: Whole report; Sections 2.2 and 5 (no blinding mentioned)

9.support: Twenty-one patients were included in the final analysis.

10.support: Repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse-Geisser correction analyzed variables during PEEP titration. Nonparametric data were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test.

11.support: Outcomes were recorded once before the recruitment maneuver and once at each PEEP step during the single decremental titration; there was no interrupted time-series design with repeated pre-intervention measurements.

12.support: The esophageal-pressure-guided PEEP titration was applied at the individual patient level, not at a group level.

nih.rationale: Strengths included a prespecified study question (item 1), clear eligibility criteria (item 2), an a priori sample-size calculation with adequate achieved power (item 5), a detailed and consistently delivered titration protocol (item 6), objectively measured and predefined outcomes (item 7), acceptable follow-up with losses accounted for (item 9), and appropriate pre-to-post statistical testing (item 10). Weaknesses lowering the rating to Fair: not all eligible participants could be enrolled and analyzed (5 of 26 excluded after enrollment; item 4), outcome assessors were unblinded and blinding was not reported (item 8), and the design lacked repeated pre-intervention measurements (item 11), leaving the physiologic pre-post comparisons vulnerable to time-related drift and measurement bias.
